label: g115-alt-canon1-vanilla1
_why: THE FIRST CENTURY ON GAME 1.15.0: the 1.15 canon beside vanilla 1.15, one run each, the same day. The user, 2026-11-08 (GAME_UPDATE_1_15 Q4): "A for now. We'll go an n=1 vs n=1 today and will see." It reads, as directions only (n=1, CLAUDE.md §2.9), what the 1.15 premise moves do to the mod over a century (Q4: wages, hiring, the productivity comparison by own type; Q5: literacy x4; Q8: the AI's pool rule) and checks the 1.15 build end to end (the research entries, the copper chain, bronze, the dams' copper, the carried AI desire, the crafts-out counts and their init tripwire). It is the first half-step of Q12's re-measure, not a replacement for it.

_arms.canon: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.g115c-canon-bz-dcu-ra-il.json} - the 1.15 canon's named copy, sha256 a52b0acacd6b6b6e (tree twin db96307af17c22ee), byte-identical to config/mod_config.json since 2026-11-08 (§10.109.5); the DEBUG build by today's emitters (L47-L49 green, the init tripwire on), telemetry v16 with the monthly downsizing poll.
_arms.vanilla: {kind: control} - vanilla 1.15.0 + telemetry v16 and nothing else.

_comparison: The canon against this batch's vanilla 1.15 run (the register's lines read by hand from the two runs: criteria.mjs's references are 1.13.11 and do not compare, CLAUDE.md §3.5); each 1.15 arm also against its 1.13.11 counterpart (F264's canon n=48, VANILLA_REF n=56) to separate what 1.15 did to vanilla from what it did to the mod. Lines: world GDP by decade; the shortlist's W, U*, H; T0 / T3 and the old-rung census (old_rungs_by_industry.mjs), the laggard test (laggard_pressure.mjs); misplaced capital; downsizing in levels by tier; the majors' technology count and literacy; red flags; play time (wall_clusters.mjs, same day, directional).

_predictions.q4_wages_hiring: Old rungs survive more than on 1.13: in the canon, T0 at 1935 / its 1900s mean above F264's 0.43, and a backward industry under a far better rung in its own market keeps more than F264's 92% of its workers over a decade. W higher and U* lower in BOTH 1.15 arms than in their 1.13 counterparts (U36's aim: an easier equilibrium at partial employment means fewer idle). Direction argued, magnitude not.
_predictions.q5_literacy: Literacy higher by 1880 in both arms than on 1.13 (x4 growth); the canon's research entries pass their literacy gates earlier, so the majors' technology count rises against F264's (Britain 160 at 1936) and vanilla 1.15's against 1.13's (77 at 1900, 107 at 1936). Direction argued.
_predictions.q8_pool: The hoard H lower than 1.13's in both arms (the new 52-week pool rule makes a construction shortfall a must-have once the pool holds a year of inflow): canon below F264's 0.24, vanilla below 0.42. Direction argued.
_predictions.register: World GDP canon / vanilla 1.15 within 0.75-1.33 (the soft band) at the end, with the 1886-1916 dip; magnitude not argued (one seed each; F264's per-run spread was 0.71-1.41).
_predictions.build: Init OK and the tripwire line 'group-level counters include child groups' in the canon's debug.log; no error.log line naming a file of ours beyond vanilla 1.15's own noise; research-entry stages complete all century; bronze artillery and copper bought; dams built with copper upkeep; save summaries written for every yearly save (the melt-tail tolerance).
_predictions.play_time: Canon within x1.10 of the same day's vanilla (directional at n=1).

_stop_rule: none: two fixed runs, both play to 1936; the stop watcher is NOT armed.
_cost: 2 x 1836 -> 1936.1.1 (~3-3.5 h each on 1.13 timings; the 1.15 probe ran 20 years in 28 min): ~6.5-7 h with builds and harvests.
_launch_checklist: setups.canon.config points at the canon's NAMED copy; nothing is canonised and no emitter, build.ps1 or tools/testbed/** file is edited until SCHEDULE DONE (L10).
Launch through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 called directly from the PowerShell tool (L30); confirm the session folder within a minute.
Five-minute smoke check on run 1 (canon: the init marker AND the tripwire line) and run 2 (vanilla).
Start the background waiter after the launch.
